The equal-budget rematch is in: plain wins reconstruction, compose wins composition.

The plain arm was resumed to epoch 99 (BSC 45051916, reached max iterations), so both arms now hold 112,500 iters. The confound the last version of this deck flagged is gone — and it was hiding the opposite ordering. Compose never leads on single-step recon, at any epoch. What it buys is LossRecon_Comp: 3.4× better, and the gap widens with training.

Plain composability decays with training. It bottoms at epoch 12 (nuScenes 0.0854) / 11 (KITTI 0.1238), then rises for 88 straight epochs to 0.1256 / 0.1693 — +47.1 % / +36.8 % off its own best. Compose is monotone down to 0.0360 / 0.0505. Composed-to-single-step ratio at ep 99: plain 3.90× / 3.71×, compose 1.09× / 1.07× and flat since epoch 11.

Visual · autoregressive rollout · KITTI

Against the GT token decode, both arms land in the same place

Scene 08_003413, both arms at epoch 99 / 112,500 iters, AR columns only, timesteps t1–t4 (t0 is the anchor and has no AR prediction). GT token is the teacher's own decode — the target the tokenizer round-trips to — and it is the same for both arms (max pixel difference 12/255 on depth, 1/255 on RGB), so one copy is shown. Both arms track it closely here; plain keeps marginally more far-field structure at t4. LossRecon_AR 0.0470 vs 0.0509 (+8.3 %).

Visual · autoregressive rollout · Occ3d-nuScenes

The shortfall to GT is far larger than anything separating the two arms

Scene scene-0017_000037, front camera of the two-camera tile, epoch 99, t1–t4. GT resolves the pedestrians as distinct figures and holds texture on the building; both arms smear them into blobs and wash out RGB contrast. That shared shortfall is the dominant effect in the frame — plain vs compose is a second-order difference on top of it. Compose is a touch softer at t4; plain holds slightly more high-frequency detail. LossRecon_AR 0.0342 vs 0.0366 (+7.0 %).

The round-trip penalty is a KITTI effect — nuScenes is near parity

plain compose 1.0 LossPointmap_PredVsOrig · from epoch 18, where the curves settle
Occ3d-nuScenes · pointmap round-trip vs epoch
KITTI · pointmap round-trip vs epoch
Round-trip = Pred vs the teacher's own recon, which removes the teacher ceiling and isolates the tokenizer. At epoch 99 compose is +3.2 % on nuScenes (0.493 vs 0.478) but +15.5 % on KITTI (0.621 vs 0.538). Plain's KITTI curve has been flat since ~epoch 25 while compose is still creeping down, so this gap is the one most likely to keep closing.

Verdict

Compose is not a reconstruction technique. It is a composability technique.

1
Neither Q1 branch holds. Compose does not merely accelerate, and it does not lower the recon floor. At equal budget plain ends 3.0 % ahead on eval recon and led at every epoch. The earlier "compose wins at 2× steps" reading was an artifact of stopping plain at epoch 49.
2
What compose actually buys. 3.4× on LossRecon_Comp, holding composed-to-single-step at ~1.08 while plain drifts to ~3.8. Price: ~3 % single-step recon, ~8 % AR recon, ~16 % KITTI geometry round-trip.
3
Plain training destroys composition. After epoch ~11 the plain arm trades composed recon for single-step recon, ending +37 % / +47 % off its own best. Training it longer makes composability worse, so the gap cannot be closed with compute.
Open
  • AR rollout does not follow composition. Compose is +8.3 % / +7.0 % worse on LossRecon_AR despite owning LossRecon_Comp. Composed ≠ autoregressive — worth understanding before treating compose as a multi-step fix.
  • Downstream flow quality. Tokenizer recon is not generation quality. The flow arms on each tokenizer — plain 44680693 vs compose 44680758 — remain the decision-grade comparison.
  • Is there a knee? Plain's composed recon bottoms at epoch 11 at 1.86× its single-step loss. A short-schedule plain tokenizer might buy most of compose's composability for free. Untested.
